$$
A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2\le x<0,\,0\le y<2}
$$

The interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,,\,0<y<2\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](images/71/71851a12f638da9604450cae0d50ed15187e850368890845d60b16b89e728bcf.png)

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](images/ab/abdd434da59bb3a1bdc0ee7de398d7ea4aeae2f617f54b5a26a5bad871ba0ac4.png)

So, in this case, the interior of $A$ is given by

$$
\text{int}\,A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-2<x<0,\,0<y<2\,}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-8f40a659-1e0d-5b32-94de-7b630e906f3f"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id - $\text{int}\,A=A$" :question/worked-solution "The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

Notice that, in this case, the set $A$ contains all of its boundary points. 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. As we've seen, $A$ contains all of its boundary points.
